purpose: Daily cross-sectional screen for statistically unusual equities across a CA+US universe, producing a max-3 watchlist with honest empty days.

output_semantics.score_pct: 0-100 percentile rank of criteria strength within the same session's eligible universe.
output_semantics.composite_z: Standard-normal score of that percentile. Sigma vs today's universe, not vs history.
output_semantics.n_qualifiers: Count of absolute own-history conditions met (0-4).
output_semantics.side: long = criteria fired to the upside, short = to the downside.
is_not: not comparable across dates in absolute terms unless universe size is stable
output_semantics.probability_shaped_numbers: Only legitimate source is a measured base rate from a point-in-time log, reported with n and standard error. See tests.score_band_base_rate.

universe.reason: Different liquidity regimes; a shared ranking lets US megacaps set the scale for TSXV names.

gates.note: Below this your own order moves the print.
Prevents fake gaps and fake RVOL.
No silent NaN propagation into the composite.

inputs.note: Distance from trend in volatility units, not percent.

inputs.formula: own_20d_return - median(20d_return of same sector, same date, same market)
inputs.note: Separates 'the sector moved' from 'this name moved'. Highest-value single input on this list.
Signed in market direction, scaled by volume excess. Strips out reversal-wick names that score well on volume and range alone: a heavy up-day closing on its low scores NEGATIVE for the long side.
Direction is a reading convention, NOT a claim that cheap outperforms.
Most-watched item on a real desk; also the most expensive data.

unscored_flags.why: Explains the unusualness; hiding it would be worse than flagging it.

unscored_flags.formula: date in economic_calendar(CPI, payrolls, FOMC, BoC, StatCan)
unscored_flags.why: RVOL spikes market-wide; without this the scanner 'discovers' that everything is unusual on CPI day.
Crowding cuts both ways. A signed weight on it would be a directional claim rather than a measurement.

unscored_flags.formula: 8-K/6-K, Form 4 / SEDI insider, 13D/G, index add-delete, lockup expiry within 3 sessions

unscored_flags.why: Signature of an unadjusted split or consolidation. Looks identical to a genuine 2-sigma move and the scanner will find it every time.

steps: magnitude inputs: rank abs(x); signed inputs: rank x
percentile = (rank - 0.5) / n, so the result is never 0 or 1 and never maps to +/-inf
fundamental inputs are multiplied by their `direction` after normalization
normalization.winsorization: none in the rank path. Clipping at the 1st/99th percentile preserves order, so it cannot change a rank. Only needed for raw-z variants.
normalization.why_ranks: One halted name with RVOL 90 hijacks a raw-z composite, and daily equity data is full of them.

composite.pillar_score: mean of that pillar's available normalized members (skip missing)
composite.raw_long: weighted mean of all pillar scores, directional pillars taken as-is
composite.raw_short: weighted mean with directional pillars sign-flipped; neutral pillars unchanged
composite.side: long if raw_long >= raw_short else short
composite.missing_pillar_handling: drop from both numerator and denominator, so weights renormalize instead of scoring a blank as neutral

restandardize.how: composite_z = inverse_normal((rank(raw within date,market) - 0.5)/n); score_pct = that percentile * 100
restandardize.why: A weighted mean of k pillars has sd about 1/sqrt(k). Thresholding the raw mean in 'sigma' is wrong by a factor of sqrt(k) -- with 9 pillars a nominal 2.0 threshold is really ~6 sigma, which in testing produced 3 picks in 150 sessions.

ceiling.why: A threshold above the ceiling returns nothing forever and looks exactly like a quiet market. Verify feasibility against universe size before blaming the criteria.

absolute_floor.why: composite_z is relative, so about 2.3% of ANY universe clears 2.0 every single session -- on 10,000 names that is 230 candidates and a top-3 list always fills. The absolute qualifiers are in own-history units, so on a quiet session nothing fires and the honest output is 'no names cleared'.

selection.max_per_sector_why: On a sector-wide move day an uncapped list returns three copies of one bet, formatted to look like three independent signals.

empty_day_target.note: Below 20% the threshold is too loose and the score has stopped meaning 'unusual'. Tighten, never loosen.

rationale: Dawes (1979), improper linear models: unit weights routinely beat regression-fitted weights out of sample because fitted weights absorb estimation error.
DeMiguel, Garlappi & Uppal (2009): naive 1/N beat optimized mean-variance out of sample across 14 datasets.
weights_policy.before_tuning: Run the sensitivity test. Perturb every weight by U(0.75, 1.25) 200 times and measure mean Jaccard overlap of the top-3 plus % of sessions where the list changed. Low overlap means the ranking is noise, and the fix is fewer pillars, not tuned weights.
weights_policy.bar_for_changing_a_weight: Must beat equal weight out-of-sample on walk-forward data, at the multiple-testing-adjusted t bar below.

tests.what: Spearman rank correlation between composite and forward return, per session, on the FULL cross-section (not just picks)
tests.fail_meaning: Mean IC around 0.30 means a lookahead bug, not an edge: verify forward returns start the session AFTER the score.

tests.source: Harvey, Liu & Zhu (2016): ~3.0 is the credible bar for a new predictor given how many have been tested. 2.0 is not enough.
tests.fail_meaning: Raise the bar further for every variant tried, and count the variants.

tests.what: pick up-rate minus the eligible universe's up-rate on the SAME sessions
tests.fail_meaning: Absolute hit rate alone is meaningless: in an up year everything hits.

tests.what: mean forward return by score decile; rank correlation of decile index vs mean return
tests.fail_meaning: Top-bucket-only effects with a flat middle are usually curve-fit.

tests.what: up-rate and mean forward return by 10-point score band, with n and binomial SE
tests.purpose: This is the only legitimate probability-shaped output: a measured base rate, never an asserted one.
tests.pass_criteria: report n and SE alongside every band; a band with few observations is not a finding

tests.what: gross minus round-trip cost (spread/2 + slippage, charged in and out)
tests.fail_meaning: A daily-turnover 3-name list is cost-heavy. In testing, 35bps ate 80% of the gross.

tests.what: perturb weights +/-25%, 200 trials, measure top-3 stability
tests.fail_meaning: Ranking is noise; reduce pillar count.

tests.what: expanding window, report only on sessions after each training window
run the whole pipeline on synthetic random-walk prices
tests.pass_criteria: mean IC ~ 0, abs(t) < 2, edge inside 2 SE, deciles non-monotone
tests.purpose: Proves the harness does not manufacture an edge. Run this before trusting any positive result.

known_limits: Horizon mismatch: documented factor premia (value, momentum, quality, low-vol) are measured on diversified, long-short, monthly-rebalanced portfolios over decades, and McLean & Pontiff (2016) found published anomaly returns decay materially post-publication. A 3-name daily list is a different statistical object -- idiosyncratic variance dominates, so even a genuine premium is invisible at that concentration and horizon. Factor literature is not support for this tool.
Small universes cannot produce large composite_z: see composite.ceiling. In a 40-name test every pick printed the same 1.96-2.16z because the top rank maps to a fixed percentile.
Regime dependence: bb_width_pct and ret_z both use trailing vol, so they misread for roughly 60 sessions after a volatility regime shift.

CA data gaps are real, not a wiring bug: effectively no usable options data, thin-to-absent analyst coverage, lagged short interest. Check pillar null rates per market before comparing a CA score to a US one.
Unadjusted corporate actions produce textbook 2-sigma moves with volume spikes. Audit before scoring.
Point-in-time discipline: a log built from back-adjusted history (e.g. yfinance) is not point-in-time and will overstate any measured edge.
